analysis.title: "This Is Basically Just One Big Trade": Goldman's Pasquariello Says It's A Bull Market, But Only If You Look In The Right Place
key_insights: Pasquariello (Goldman head of hedge fund coverage) keeps the call that the primary trend is up for the S&P and NDX, but his latest note is more two-sided and he no longer says the next 5% is up. He advises clients to 'mind the speed limit'.
The S&P closed at a new high of 7,818 on Tuesday, then fell to 7,765 on Thursday after an OpenAI revenue scare. The index had been pinned near 7,700 for about two months.

Breadth is extremely narrow. Nearly half of S&P members carry a negative beta to the index (45% on a three-month basis per Goldman's Brian Garrett, an all-time high). The article says one in six S&P members is in a 50%+ drawdown.

Since Aug 27 the S&P is up 1.28% while the S&P ex-AI (SPXXAI) is down 5.19% (Adrien Simonet). The Russell 2000 has lagged the Nasdaq in 16 of the past 20 sessions by about 9 percentage points (Rikin Shah).

Positioning is light in aggregate. Goldman Prime Book net exposure to US equities is at 1, 3 and 5 year lows, fundamental L/S net leverage fell three weeks running to the lowest since Liberation Day, and US fundamental L/S net length is in the 1st percentile of the past year (Mark Wilson).

Gross exposure is high and the remaining net is concentrated. Tech was the only sector hedge funds bought in September (largest monthly buying since February 2025). Mag 7 is about 22% of total US exposure on the Prime Book, a record since 2022, and semis are 12%, double the start of the year.

Levered semis ETF assets are about $115 billion (Simonet), which would amplify a move lower. Goldman's TMT desk saw more than $1 billion of net supply in semis, AI and megacap tech on Thursday after the OpenAI headline.

Pasquariello's third claim: Q3 S&P earnings growth of about 28% y/y (27% in Goldman's Ben Snider preview and in Monday's note). Median S&P stock growth is expected to slow from 14% in Q2 to 9% in Q3. Sector growth is tech +64% and energy +122%.

Top 10 contributors will generate 68% of S&P EPS growth this quarter, up from 48% last quarter, and Micron and Nvidia account for half of that 68% (Wilson). Goldman's 27% estimate is the cycle high, with growth decelerating in each of the next three quarters, and hyperscaler capex growth (116% per Snider) is likely to peak this quarter.

Concentration chart (Dan Chavez): the 10 largest companies are 41% of S&P market cap versus 38% of S&P earnings. The gap was about 12 points at the 2000 peak and is three points now. The article notes this is trailing earnings, partly one hyperscaler's capex becoming another's revenue.

Rates are now framed as a bigger risk to sovereigns and corporates, a step up from 'a headwind and not a wrecking ball' ten days earlier. The 30Y auction stopped at 5.618%, the highest since August 2000, and the 10Y closed at 5.23%.

The Fed under Warsh hiked in September to 3.75%-4% and Goldman economists expect another hike in December. Shah calculates that 98bp of the 108bp selloff in 10Y yields came from real rates, with 30Y real yields at 3.33%, near the top of the post-2010 range.

Goldman credit strategists are watching for the point where rates become a net headwind for credit, and single out software issuers with loan maturities to refinance. USD IG has returned -292bp year to date. Goldman economists estimate current rate levels could subtract 0.5pp from 2027 growth.

Simonet warns a term-premium shock reprices all long-dated cash flows regardless of AI quality. The left tail is a Fed forced to hike more than expected to defend long-end credibility, with CPI as the near-term trigger.
Claim 5: 'this is basically just one big trade', a quote from an investor, which Pasquariello does not dispute. Zero Hedge argues that trend, positioning, earnings and rates all trace back to AI.
A 50/50 composite of tech and energy has been up in 10 of the past 11 years, averaging 18.7% a year with a Sharpe of 1.2.

Claim 6: Q4 seasonals are friendlier but midterms (Nov 3) may bring volatility. Prediction markets give Democrats over 90% for the House and 65% for the Senate (Alec Phillips), with an 8.9pp generic ballot lead. The VIX closed Thursday at 15.4 and a buyer of about $10 million of vega in year-end S&P puts traded over six hours.

Pasquariello's conclusions: stay long but near-term risk/reward is unclear, stay with the US and Japan, and pair long equities with a paid rates position. His speculative length score was +3 on a -10 to +10 scale on Sep 25.

Japan: TOPIX up 20% YTD in local terms against about 12% for the S&P, Nikkei up more than 36%. Goldman Japan strategists say ex-banks and AI hardware, TOPIX is up only 8% since the Takaichi administration began.

Zero Hedge's view: the bull case needs Micron and Nvidia to deliver, hyperscaler capex not to peak, the Fed to stop at two hikes and the long bond to find a buyer at 5.6%. The bear case needs one of those to miss. Zero Hedge's next check is after hyperscaler earnings in the last week of October.

sector_views.rationale: Pasquariello says stay long the US mega cap tech engine and the AI complex. Tech earnings growth is +64% and tech was the only sector hedge funds bought in September, but positioning is concentrated.
Energy earnings growth is +122% and a 50/50 tech and energy composite has been up in 10 of 11 years, averaging 18.7% a year.
They are described as getting hammered by rising yields while mega cap tech leads. The S&P ex-AI is down 5.19% since Aug 27.
Goldman credit strategists single out software issuers with loan maturities to refinance as exposed to high rates.

earnings_insights: Q3 S&P EPS growth is about 28% y/y per Pasquariello (estimate, up from 27% in Monday's note and in Snider's Q3 preview). Goldman's 27% estimate is the cycle high, with growth decelerating in each of the next three quarters.
Consensus growth for the median S&P stock is expected to slow from 14% in Q2 to 9% in Q3 (Snider preview, estimate).
Sector Q3 growth estimates: tech +64%, energy +122% (Pasquariello, estimates).
The top 10 contributors are expected to generate 68% of S&P EPS growth in Q3, up from 48% in Q2, and Micron (MU) and Nvidia (NVDA) account for half of the 68% (Wilson, estimate).

Hyperscaler capex growth is running above 100% (Snider: 116%) and is likely to peak in Q3 (estimate). Earnings season starts the week of Oct 12 and about 70% of S&P market cap will have reported by the last week of October.

Near the top of the post-2010 range.
The Fed under Warsh hiked in September.
Goldman economists expect a further hike. Simonet sees the risk as a Fed hiking more than expected, with CPI as the trigger.
Rates at multi-decade highs are pressuring credit, and strategists are watching for rates to become a net headwind.

trade_ideas.description: Long US equities paired with a paid (short bond) rates position
trade_ideas.rationale: Nominal growth stays higher for longer, which is good for profits and bad for bonds, given a $2 trillion deficit and $1 trillion of AI capex.
trade_ideas.risk: A paid rates leg only pays if yields keep rising, which hurts the 85% of the index already underwater (Zero Hedge's critique).

trade_ideas.description: Stay long the US and Japan equities, 'the two fastest horses in the race'
trade_ideas.rationale: TOPIX is up 20% YTD in local terms and the Nikkei more than 36%, against about 12% for the S&P, but ex-banks and AI hardware TOPIX is up only 8% since the Takaichi administration began.
trade_ideas.risk: Japan's strength is the same AI hardware trade as the US, so it does not diversify.

trade_ideas.description: Own a 50/50 composite of tech and energy sectors
trade_ideas.rationale: It has been up in 10 of the past 11 years, averaging 18.7% a year with a Sharpe of 1.2.

risk_factors: Rising long-end yields: the 30Y auction at 5.618% and 10Y at 5.23% raise the risk to sovereigns and corporates, and a term-premium shock reprices tech and AI regardless of quality.
A Fed forced to hike more than expected to defend long-end credibility, with CPI as the near-term trigger.
Concentration: one trade (AI) drives trend, earnings, positioning and funding needs, and Micron and Nvidia account for much of the earnings growth.
Peak earnings growth and peak hyperscaler capex growth may arrive together this quarter.
Levered semis ETF assets of about $115 billion could amplify a selloff, and Thursday's OpenAI revenue scare produced over $1 billion of net supply in semis, AI and megacap tech.
Narrow breadth: nearly half of S&P members have negative beta to the index and about one in six are in a 50%+ drawdown.
Credit stress for software issuers with loan maturities to refinance, and for IG broadly if rates become a net headwind.
Midterm-election volatility around Nov 3, with a Democratic sweep now the modal outcome in prediction markets.
Sovereign funding competition from the AI investment cycle, including about $150 billion of chip debt issued in roughly a week.

geopolitical: US midterm elections on Nov 3: prediction markets give Democrats over 90% odds of taking the House and 65% for the Senate, and Pasquariello expects midterm-related volatility.
France sovereign financing: Shah notes marginal financing cost is about 250bp above the effective rate on the existing debt stock.

cross_bank_references: Goldman's Prime Book, TMT desk, vol desk, credit strategists, economists and Japan strategists are all cited within the Pasquariello note coverage.
Zero Hedge relays Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson warning that bad breadth 'must be resolved one way or another' (Oct 4).

tension_points.bull_case: The primary trend is up for the S&P and NDX, positioning is at multi-year lows, Q3 EPS growth is about 28%, and the top 10 stocks' share of earnings (38%) is close to their share of market cap (41%).
tension_points.bear_case: Rising yields (30Y at 5.618%, 10Y at 5.23%), narrow breadth, a record Mag 7 weight, peak earnings growth and capex growth arriving together, and one trade as the source of trend, earnings and funding stress.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A miss by Micron or Nvidia, hyperscaler capex peaking, the Fed hiking more than twice, or the long bond failing to find a buyer at 5.6%.

tension_points.bull_case: Higher rates were previously a headwind and not a wrecking ball, and nominal growth staying higher for longer supports profits, so a paid rates position hedges equity length.
tension_points.bear_case: A term-premium shock reprices all long-dated cash flows and a Fed forced to hike more than expected could break the long end and credit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hot CPI print forcing the Fed to hike more than expected.

theme_stances.key_argument: Mega cap tech must carry the whole market, so the ante has gone up and this is basically one big trade.
theme_stances.evidence: this is basically just one big trade, don't you?

theme_stances.key_argument: Higher rates are becoming a bigger risk to both sovereigns and corporates, and a term-premium shock hits good and mediocre AI stories alike.
Trading community length is conspicuously low, so upside calls are cheap and positioning is not a barrier to higher prices.
